label: Molecules have no up: rotation and translation
context: A small molecule/protein fragment of 10 atoms as a 2D ball-and-stick drawing. Phase 1: rotate and translate it smoothly around the canvas; caption 'same structure in any pose'. Phase 2 'equivariant denoiser (RFdiffusion)': show a noisy version with predicted correction arrows on each atom; as the whole thing rotates, the arrows rotate with it rigidly. Phase 3 'augmentation (AlphaFold 3)': during 'training' many randomly rotated and shifted copies flash briefly (faint), caption 'AF3 uses a plain transformer and random rotations instead: it learns the symmetry from data'. Phase 4: one residue drawn as a frame: a Cα dot with two small orthogonal axis arrows, caption 'RFdiffusion's state: one rigid frame (position + rotation) per residue'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Molecules have no up: rotation and translation
spec.caption: A 10-atom fragment moves freely, so any pose is the same structure. An equivariant denoiser's correction arrows rotate rigidly with the molecule. AlphaFold 3 instead learns the symmetry from randomly rotated and shifted copies. RFdiffusion represents each residue as a rigid frame (t, R).
